title: He won battles…
paragraphs:
He won battles…
but one small defeat exposed everything.

Not the enemy.
Not the numbers.
Not the strategy.
And suddenly, the strong man was on the ground—tearing his clothes like his soul was coming apart.

Because sometimes the collapse you’re blaming on life…
is actually God exposing what you refused to confront.

Because Joshua didn’t fall apart at Jericho.
He fell apart at Ai.

A smaller battle.
A weaker enemy.
An easier win.
And that’s what makes this dangerous.
Because it’s not always the big, obvious sins that take you down.

The private compromises.
The quiet disobedience.
The thing you told yourself, “It’s not a big deal.”
He just knew something was wrong.
So he did what many of us don’t do anymore.

He didn’t scroll.
He didn’t blame.
He didn’t spin the narrative.
“Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell to the earth on his face before the ark of the LORD until the evening… and put dust on their heads.” (Joshua 7:6)

That’s a man realizing:
“God is not with us the way He was… and something is deeply broken.”
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
“Alas, O Lord GOD, why have you brought this people over the Jordan at all…?” (Joshua 7:7)

When things fall apart and your first instinct is not repentance…
but accusation?

“God, why did You allow this?”
“God, where were You?”
“God, why is this happening to me?”
“Get up! Why have you fallen on your face? Israel has sinned…” (Joshua 7:10–11)
but God was pointing to sin.
but God was exposing the cause.

You can be emotional…
you can be sincere…
you can even be praying…
and still be avoiding the real issue.
There was a man named Achan.
And that secret sin didn’t stay private.

Sin whispers,
“This is just between you and me.”

But Scripture screams,
“Your sin will find you out.” (Numbers 32:23)
And some scholars interpret this moment not just as individual failure, but as covenant responsibility—Israel was one people before God, and hidden sin had corporate consequences.

That means your “small” compromise…
your “private” habit…
your “no one will know” decision…

Into your spirit.
Into your decisions.
Into your relationships.
Into your calling.
But He also restored His people.
Because God is not just holy.
But mercy is never found in denial.
This whole moment is pointing forward.
Joshua fell to the ground because of sin in the camp.
But there would come another Joshua—Jesus.
And He wouldn’t fall because of His sin.
He would fall under the weight of ours.
Joshua tore his clothes in grief.
Jesus had His clothes torn from Him in sacrifice.

Joshua cried out,
“What will You do for Your great name?” (Joshua 7:9)
Jesus answered that question on the cross.
He upheld the holiness of God…
and made a way for sinners to come home.
This is repentance—honest, raw, turning back.
This is grace—undeserved, costly, offered freely.
You don’t fix what Ai exposed.
You bring it to the cross.
You stop pretending you’re still winning when your soul is losing.

God will expose what you won’t surrender—
not to destroy you…
but to save you.
What have you buried under layers of excuses?
What have you labeled “normal” that God calls sin?
Not to feel bad and move on.
Come back to God—not polished, not perfect, but honest.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)
But only if you come into the light.
Because the same God who exposed the sin in Joshua’s camp…
is the same God who sent His Son to carry yours.
And Jesus didn’t die so you could keep hiding.
He died so you could be free.

Free from guilt.
Free from bondage.
Free from pretending.
And receive the mercy you’ve been running from.
